clue.text: Press people help imprisoned group

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them

indicators.note: imprisoned means one word is locked up inside the word for people

parts.note: men is a common crossword stand-in for people
aid means help

explanation.surface: Reporters assist a band of people who have been jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists, but it is the verb for smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Maiden is a British heavy-metal band, so it is a musical group.

clue.text: Theatrical duke's assets turned theatre round

parts.note: pros are advantages or plus points, i.e. assets

indicators.note: turned means the theatre word is flipped end to end

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A stage nobleman's wealth has transformed the playhouse around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' flips REP to PER. Prospero, the magician of Shakespeare's The Tempest, is the rightful Duke of Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero is a duke who exists only on stage, in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Order cream — what's in it?

indicators.note: in it means the word for what goes inside the word for cream

parts.note: the cream of something is the best of it
eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard

explanation.surface: Someone orders cream and asks suspiciously what is in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's' splits as 'what' plus 'is'; 'in it' points back to the cream word.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or request, as in 'at the king's behest', so it is an order.

clue.text: King stops to shoot crow

indicators.note: stops means the king plugs the middle of the shooting word, like a stopper

parts.note: to bag game is to shoot it
R (Rex) is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch halts to fire at a black bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' looks like the bird, which fits the shooting picture, but it is the verb to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast loudly about a success, which is what bragging means.

clue.text: After fighting, Archers' cat gets cards

indicators.note: after a fight things are in disarray, so these letters are left jumbled

parts.note: the letters of archers, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Following a scrap, the archers' cat acquires playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cards' looks like playing cards, but here it means eccentric people.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an amusing eccentric, and so is a character; both are informal labels for odd people.

clue.text: See 24
Boss's moon in workshop

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface
Io is one of the moons of Jupiter

explanation.surface: The manager's moon is kept in his workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but it is the ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is an artist's or craftsperson's workroom, a kind of workshop.

clue.text: Garden party is chance to talk

indicators.note: to talk means the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: fate is fortune or chance

explanation.surface: An outdoor gathering is an opportunity for a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fundraising event, typically held on a lawn, like a garden party.

clue.text: No common ground — it's elementary

parts.note: something rare is not common
earth is ground or soil

explanation.surface: Uncommon ground is explained away as simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's elementary' sounds like 'it's simple' but means it is a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare earths are a group of metallic chemical elements, so one is literally elementary.

clue.text: Hit with fine out on call — policy open to criticism

indicators.note: out means the letters of the two words are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
to ring someone is to call them
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: Someone struck with a penalty while on call finds the policy attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HIT and FINE into INTHEFI.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the firing line means being the target of attack or blame, so open to criticism.

clue.text: Receives inside information about savings

indicators.note: about means the combined letters are turned round
inside means the receiving word sits within the information word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
gets means receives

explanation.surface: Someone is fed insider tips about a savings scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside information' reads as one phrase, but it splits across two jobs; 'about' turns the whole result round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside for the future, a sum of savings.

clue.text: Balance on turning is outstanding

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: turning means the little word is flipped round

parts.note: a debt outstanding is still due

explanation.surface: The amount left on a bank statement is shown as overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: The residue is what remains, and so is the balance of an amount.

clue.text: Warn distant relative over display

indicators.note: over means the found letters are read backwards
display means the letters are on show inside the two words

explanation.surface: Caution a far-off kinsman about putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' shows TRELA in 'distanT RELAtive'; 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert someone is to warn them of danger; both are verbs of giving notice.

clue.text: Used chops past their sell-by date? Not happy

parts.note: to hack is to use chopping strokes, so hacked means chopped
food that has gone off is past its sell-by date

explanation.surface: A butcher's lamb chops are stale, and the customer is unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chops' looks like a noun (meat) but is the verb, and 'Used' is past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacked off is informal British for annoyed, i.e. thoroughly displeased.

clue.text: After a short time, follow rivals around church

indicators.note: after means the next part follows the shortened time in the answer
short means the time word loses its final letter

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

indicators.note: around means the following-and-rivals letters are turned round

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
foes are enemies or rivals

explanation.surface: After a brief wait, trail competitors round a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the follow-plus-rivals pair into SEOFGOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A house of God is a place of worship, so a church.

clue.text: See 10
Old privilege of rank sure intrigued? Do elaborate!

indicators.note: to elaborate is to work something into a more complex form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historic aristocratic right sounds intriguing; please explain more.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is French, 'right of the lord', supposedly letting a feudal lord sleep with a vassal's bride.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the alleged medieval right of a feudal lord, an ancient privilege of high status.

clue.text: Briefly flash queen wearing one's hat

indicators.note: briefly means the instant word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: in a trice, in a flash: both mean an instant

indicators.note: wearing means the number word has the queen inside it, as if worn

parts.note: taken as written
R (Regina) is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: The queen quickly flashes the hat she is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims TRICE to TRIC; 'wearing' puts R in ONE to make ORNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorne is a three-cornered hat of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Clear in past — parking permitted

parts.note: ex means former, from the past
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: It was obvious in the past that parking was allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated plainly, leaving no doubt, so clear.

clue.text: Once virtue finally gone, sense saint might show it

definitions.text: Once virtue finally gone, sense saint might show it

indicators.note: gone means that closing letter is removed from the pool of letters
might show it means the letters can be rearranged to reveal the result
finally means only the closing letter of virtue is used

explanation.surface: Once a saint's goodness has faded, spite could appear.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle SENSE SAINT, then remove E, the end of 'virtue'. Read whole, the clue also describes the result: a saint stripped of virtue shows spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastiness is spitefulness, just what a saint who had lost all virtue would display.

clue.text: Doctor calls scurvy ultimately a danger to sailors

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of scurvy is taken

explanation.surface: A medic says scurvy was eventually a threat to seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician, which suits scurvy, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Scylla is the sea monster of Greek myth that snatched sailors from passing ships.

clue.text: Mature player originally employed by French FA

indicators.note: employed by means the letter is taken inside the French word

parts.note: sweet FA is British slang for nothing, and rien is French for nothing

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of player

explanation.surface: An experienced footballer is first signed by the French Football Association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'FA' looks like the Football Association, but 'sweet FA' is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to mature, as fruit does.

clue.text: Is that right about colleague fighting?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an ally is a partner fighting on your side

explanation.surface: A doubter asks whether a coworker really is brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: Really? is a reply expressing surprise, the same as asking whether something is true.

clue.text: Keen to meet Lothario, tell an alarming lie

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
a Lothario is a womaniser, and so is a wolf

explanation.surface: A mourner meets a seducer and spins a frightening falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager but is the verb to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry wolf is to raise a false alarm, from the fable of the shepherd boy.

clue.text: Clubs taken in country

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
had means taken, as in had a biscuit

explanation.surface: Golf clubs are seized in some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Fan in slap keeping close to Joe Cocker?

indicators.note: keeping means the shuffled letters hold that final letter inside
to fan things out is to spread them around, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: An admirer gets slapped while holding on to the singer Joe Cocker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a devotee of Joe Cocker but is the anagram signal; 'keeping' puts E inside the jumble. The question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocker is a breed of spaniel, so it defines the dog by example.

clue.text: Cut, saying nothing at first

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of nothing

explanation.surface: Edited, with nothing said at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawn is the past participle of saw, so it means cut with a saw.

clue.text: Quite — beginner's struggling with German poet

parts.note: all can mean quite or completely, as in all alone

indicators.note: struggling means the letters writhe into a new order

parts.note: the letters of beginners, taken as written

explanation.surface: A novice battles with a German poet, quite literally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges BEGINNERS into ENGINSBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Allen Ginsberg was the American Beat poet who wrote Howl.

clue.text: Brown allies as a body angered by Blair

indicators.note: angered means the letters are stirred up into a new order
as a body means only the body of the word survives, so its outside letters go

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's supporters together were furious with Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angered' shuffles BROWN ALLIES into BORWELLIANS; 'as a body' keeps the middle, dropping B and S. George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair, so 'by Blair' means in Orwell's manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Blair wrote as George Orwell, so something by Blair belongs to Orwell's work or style.
